newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.86/87 as dlr demand spurts.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.86/87 as dlr demand spurts.

text.p: The rupee ended at 35.86/87 against the dollar on Tuesday amid the first faint signs of a rally in dollar demand seen in the new year, dealers said.
The dollar was quoted at a high of 35.87/88 after opening the day at 35.86/87 as dealers went long on dollars reacting to aggressive dollar buying by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday.
Some dealers said it was too early to say whether dollar demand had risen to a level to force a much-needed correction in the rupee-dollar exchange rate which has been stable for long.
"There was some corporate buying today," said a dealer. "But most importers are still not covering (their dollar requirements) seeing the rupee's stability," he said.
The rupee revived to 35.85/86 level in January after touching a low of 35.95 against the dollar in December 1996.
Premia continued to be under pressure in the forward dollar market because of abnormally low call money rates.
The six-month annualised premium closed Tuesday at 7.03 percent compared to Monday's 7.14 percent closing, dealers said.
